Discrete Diffusion Models (DDMs) transfer this idea by operating directly on the discrete state space ( Austin et al., 2021 ; Shi et al., 2024 ; Campbell et al., 2022 ) , as an alternative to embedding tokens into a continuous latent space and reusing continuous machinery ( Dieleman et al., 2022 ) . Like their continuous counterparts, DDMs progressively corrupt data, either by masking tokens or by replacing them with tokens drawn uniformly from the vocabulary. In the discrete setting, the score function is replaced by a rate function R t ​ ( x , y ) R_{t}(x,y) , the instantaneous probability of token y y transitioning to token x x . Integrating this rate over diffusion time defines a continuous time Markov chain. This process, like in the continuous case, carries the state from noise to data ( Campbell et al., 2022 ; Gat et al., 2024 ) . Emerging evidence in language and DNA modeling suggests that DDMs could rival autoregressive models, thanks to their bidirectional context and multi-token generation ( Nie et al., 2025 ; Stark et al., 2024 ; Sahoo et al., 2026 ) . Yet, while the literature on continuous diffusion models has extensively explored noise schedules ( Karras et al., 2022 ; Stancevic et al., 2025 ) , training dynamics ( Karras et al., 2024b ) , and inference-time guidance ( Dhariwal and Nichol, 2021 ; Ho and Salimans, 2021 ) , the algorithmic tools for discrete diffusion, and in particular for guiding it, remain far less developed. We address this gap by transferring to the discrete setting two guidance tools that have no discrete counterpart yet: the online tracking of the class posterior during generation, and the composition of conditional generative processes through logical operators. Classifier-free guidance (CFG) ( Dhariwal and Nichol, 2021 ; Ho and Salimans, 2021 ) applies a constant push towards a condition throughout the denoising process, regardless of whether the considered sample needs it. Recent work in continuous diffusion has shown that guidance can instead adapt to the state of the trajectory, only being used if a trajectory truly requires it ( Koulischer et al., 2025a ; Koulischer et al., 2025b ; Galashov et al., 2025 ) . Additionally, guidance can be used for composing several conditional generative processes, for instance to generate samples satisfying either or both of two conditions. This requires weighting each process according to how likely the current state is to satisfy its corresponding condition ( Skreta et al., 2025 ; Alesiani et al., 2026 ) . All of these constructions rely on the same quantity, the class posterior p t ​ ( c ∣ x t ) p_{t}(c\mid x_{t}) , which estimates the probability that the noisy state x t x_{t} will eventually satisfy condition c c . In this work, we focus on how conditional and unconditional model predictions, and their corresponding rate functions, can be combined to estimate this posterior and construct different conditional generative processes. We show that the class posterior can be tracked during discrete diffusion directly from the conditional and unconditional predictions, for both uniform and masking noise. The estimation is exact when analytical quantities are available and exhibits interpretable token-level dynamics: because the state changes one token at a time, transitions that support a class increase its posterior, while transitions supporting a different class decrease it. This provides a direct interpretation of the posterior that has no continuous analogue. In masked language modeling, for example, it reveals which generated tokens move a sample towards or away from a class. Building on this posterior estimation, we extend CFG to the logical and , or , and not operators for discrete rate functions, drawing on recent advances in the continuous domain ( Alesiani et al., 2026 ; Skreta et al., 2025 ; Koulischer et al., 2025a ) . These operators combine conditional rate functions through posterior-dependent weighting: the or gate arbitrates between the conditions according to their posterior probabilities, while the not gate detects the undesired condition and activates a repulsive term only when necessary. We verify these constructions analytically and validate them on discrete image and antibody sequence generation. Our derivation also reveals that standard discrete CFG ( Schiff et al., 2025 ; Nisonoff et al., 2025 ) differs from its continuous counterpart in a way that has gone unnoticed. Continuous CFG mixes marginals multiplicatively, which is realized as an additive mixture of predictions, whereas discrete CFG instead mixes data distributions multiplicatively. These operations are not equivalent because the noising process does not commute with multiplicative mixing ( Bradley and Nakkiran, 2024 ) . Our contributions are threefold: 1. we cast the online class posterior to the discrete domain and demonstrate its interpretable dynamics in language generation; 2. we derive posterior-weighted or and not operators for discrete rate functions, verify these on an analytical example, and validate on discrete image generation and antibody sequence generation; and 3. we identify and formalize the multiplicative/additive mismatch between continuous and discrete CFG. Recent progress on guidance: Both formulations have since been refined. In the continuous case it was proposed to schedule the guidance scale λ \lambda over time rather than hold it fixed, aiming to target the noise levels that benefit most from it ( Kynkäänniemi et al., 2024 ; Koulischer et al., 2025b ; Galashov et al., 2025 ) . More recently, guidance has been reframed as one instance of a broader family of operators for combining diffusion processes, including and (both conditions), or (either condition) and not (avoid a condition) ( Skreta et al., 2025 ; Koulischer et al., 2025a ; Alesiani et al., 2026 ) . Conclusion We have shown that the class-conditional posterior in discrete diffusion can be tracked online, at no cost beyond the conditional and unconditional predictions already required for guidance. In diffusion language modeling this posterior is highly interpretable: individual tokens can be seen to commit a sample toward a class or away from it during generation. Building on the posterior, we derived the and , or , and not operators over discrete rate functions, providing a principled means of composing conditional processes. The not gate is of particular practical value, enabling generation that steers away from a class in modalities such as images and antibody sequences, where prompting a model to avoid a concept is not possible. As the construction is agnostic to modality, noising process, data imbalances and schedules, it applies unchanged across the settings we consider. The derivation additionally revealed a previously unremarked discrepancy between classifier-free guidance in the continuous domain, an additive mixture of scores, and the discrete domain, a multiplicative mixture of predictions.
